source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
OCB1 publishes 9 MW of IT capacity across 420,000 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 9 MW supports roughly 225 racks; at a more modest 10 kW per rack, typical of general colocation, the same power supports around 900 racks. The operator has not published a rack count, a power-use-effectiveness figure, or a stated design density, so the actual configuration is not known from the spec page alone.

The five certifications tell a specific story about workload eligibility. PCI DSS qualifies the campus to host payment-card processing environments. HIPAA and HITRUST together qualify it for regulated healthcare data. FISMA qualifies it for federal information systems subject to that framework. TIA-942 is a facilities-design standard, not a security or compliance regime, and its presence signals that the physical infrastructure was designed and audited against a formal tier methodology. None of these certifications indicate AI training workloads are present or absent; they indicate what compliance postures a tenant can satisfy here.

Iowa has 52 facilities mapped in this site's data, and only one, this campus, has a published megawatt figure. OCB1 therefore ranks first in Iowa by published IT capacity, but that ranking reflects the absence of published data from other operators rather than a confirmed dominance of the state's actual installed base. Nine megawatts is a modest figure relative to the hundred-plus-megawatt campuses now being announced for AI infrastructure elsewhere in the Midwest, and nothing in the published specifications indicates a planned expansion.
